"In watery worlds too small to see, 
weird little guys live in a weird little world.

Eight chubby legs reach out & plod,
Through thick green strings of algae sod.

With heavy steps & clumsy grace,
He plows across this tiny place." 

- @c0nc0rdance on Bluesky

📹: Sinclair Stammer Science Photo Library

Tardigrades are commonly known as water bears or moss piglets. They are found in practically every habitat on Earth, from hot springs to beneath ice sheets, and are renowned for their toughness. 

Experiments have shown they can survive being frozen to nearly absolute zero and heated to 150° Celsius. They have survived pressures of more than 6000 atmospheres, and have survived after prolonged exposure to the vacuum and radiation found in space. 

In unfavourable conditions they can dehydrate to 1% of their normal water content and remain alive in stasis for over a decade. In more normal conditions, they prefer moist environments where they feed on algae and bacteria.
